title: Vanishing of the higher direct images above the dimension
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $d\in\mathbf N$, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes with $\dim X\leq d$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite-type morphism, and let $A$ be a finite commutative coefficient ring annihilated by an integer invertible in $k$. Then the higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] satisfy
$$R^qf_*M=0\qquad(q>2d)$$
for every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on $X_{\Et}$. Separatedness of $f$ is not needed. In the global finite-field and coefficient-stage setting, and for separated $f$, to which [def-sf-uniform-direct-image-vanishing] applies, this asserts $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;2d)$. The dimension is the topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and finite type has the meaning of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: Since $k$ is algebraically closed, every finite separable extension is trivial, so $k$ is separably closed by [def-kun-separably-closed]. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type, and the given structure morphism $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Equip $X$ with the structure map $a_X=a_Y\circ f$; then the required compatibility is an equality by construction. No agreement of this map with an initially supplied $k$-structure on $X$ is needed: its underlying scheme and dimension have not changed. Finally, if $n>0$ annihilates $A$, then $na=0$ for every $a\in A$, so the additive group of $A$ is torsion, including when $A$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 01T1 (definition-finite-type), items (2)–(3), in Tag 01T0 (section-finite-type); elementary hypothesis checks for the relative bound

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-relative-torsion-direct-image-dimension-bound] with $\Lambda=A$, the maps $a_X,a_Y$ just chosen, the given $d$, and any sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. Step 1 verifies the separably closed ground field, torsion additive coefficient group, quasi-compactness and local finite type of $f$, local finite type of $a_Y$, and compatibility of structure maps. The remaining hypothesis is exactly $\dim X\leq d$. Its conclusion gives $R^q f_*M=0$ for every $q>2d$. This is a theorem about module higher direct images themselves, so no identification of module and abelian derived functors is being assumed. The cited theorem has no separatedness, properness, constructibility or invertibility requirement; consequently it applies with all of the present hypotheses, including to empty $X$.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1–4: torsion cohomological-dimension argument, reused through the existing stronger relative bound

proof.text: The preceding conclusion quantifies over every $A$-module sheaf and every $q>2d$. When the global finite-field datum, coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$ and separated finite-type $f$ required by [def-sf-uniform-direct-image-vanishing] are present, substitute $N=2d$ into that definition. Its defining vanishing condition is exactly the conclusion of step 2, hence $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;2d)$ holds in that setting.
